mu_name_from: MuMain loads glove indexes 10 to 14 from GloveElf{i+1}, not GloveMale (ZzzOpenData.cpp line 151: `AccessModel(MODEL_GLOVES + i + 10, ..., L"GloveElf", i + 1)`), so index 10 is GloveElf01, which openmu's 0.75 Armors.cs names the Vine Gloves. mu.db agrees: code 5130, group 10 index 10, Player/GloveElf01.bmd. There is no GloveMale11 on disk, which is how the numbering was noticed.
why_this_one:
One of the four pieces of armour a Budge Dragon can leave, and the Elf's: the Vine set is hers as Pad is the wizard's and Leather the knight's. Drop level 4, the dragon's own, so it falls plain.

The first Elf-set part in the tree, and the file naming is the thing worth knowing about it: the Male files run to index 9 and the five elf sets are a second series with their own prefix.
profile_from: Not armour, whose default is plate_steel. See profiles/soft_armour.json.

stats.note: The item's own row, copied from OpenMU's 0.75 initialiser rather than restated, with the call it came from beside it.
stats.from: openmu/src/Persistence/Initialization/Version075/Items/Armors.cs line 114. The 0.75 table, which is the version this server is being built to.
stats.call_note: ArmorInitializerBase.CreateGloves(number, name, dropLevel, defense, attackSpeed, durability, strengthRequirement, agilityRequirement, darkWizardClassLevel, darkKnightClassLevel, elfClassLevel). Slot 5, so `armor.Group = (byte)(slot + 5)` makes the group 10.
stats.drop_level_note: Four, the Budge Dragon's own level. In the pool at +0 and out of it for anything smaller. See shared/Loot.Affordable.
stats.attack_speed_note: Four, half the Leather Gloves' eight. Recorded and unread: shared/Combat.cs takes attack speed off the weapon row alone.
stats.defense_note: Two points of defence, in the row and not read by anything yet. Flagged rather than left to look implemented.
stats.classes_from: The last three ints of the call are 0, 0, 1 - the Elf alone. The only piece in the dragon's pool with an agility gate, sixty, which is the Elf set's shape throughout.

sheet_from: Data/Player/gloves_04c.OZJ (64x64) and Data/Player/hide.jpg, from MuMain. The .bmd names gloves_04c.jpg and hide.jpg; 146 of the 152 triangles are on the first and 6 on the second. The `c` is MU's own suffix for the elf recolour of the 04 sheet - the Pad Gloves' gloves_04 is the same layout in violet and gold.
sheet_note:
A dark brown bracer from two sides, mean (69, 43, 30): tooled bronze-brown scrollwork over darker hide, black straps across the wrist and a fringe of small gilt tassels at the bottom edge, on a dull red-brown ground. Warmer and much darker than the Pad sheet it shares a layout with, and the ornament is raised leather rather than a metal plate - the highlights are the same brown lifted, not a different colour.

hide is MU capping the openings, a 9x9 solid black, as on ArmorMale10.
material_note: leather on both islands, which is the profile's default and here it is also the answer. The sheet is dark hide with the scrollwork raised in the same brown - the highlights are the leather lifted, not a metal laid on it - so unlike the Pad Gloves, whose layout this shares, there is no plate to argue for brass. The gilt tassels at the wrist and the black straps are a few texels each on an island that is otherwise all hide; the island is the unit, and majority is not close.
